score.description: Overall quality of the journey: how smoothly the app let the user succeed.

completion.description: Did the user accomplish what the story asked?

assessment.description: Step count vs. what the task should take; backtracking; hesitation.

wasted_steps.description: Steps that did not advance the task.

step.description: Step number the finding refers to, if specific.

findings.description: Free-form UX/quality observations, e.g. 'the error message after an invalid card is blank'.

summary.description: The report a developer reads first: what happened, how smooth it felt, and what to look at. Detail is welcome; format it with newlines into a one-line verdict plus a few short points — readable, never one dense block. The findings carry the per-issue specifics.

question.description: The report question, quoted verbatim from the case.

answer.description: The answer, grounded in the trajectory.

evidence_steps.description: Step numbers that evidence the answer.

report.description: Answers to the case's report questions, one entry per question, in order. Present only when the case declares report questions.

a11y.description: HARNESS-COMPUTED accessibility summary (NOT grader-authored) — exact axe-core counts spread onto the grade after the LLM call, for compliance. Present only when the run carried axe captures (web). The grader sees a short digest of this in its prompt so findings can reference a11y, but it never writes these numbers.

total_violations.description: Total violation NODE count across all steps (full-page runs) — what accessibility_violations gates on.

steps_with_violations.description: How many steps had at least one violation.

top_rules.description: The most frequently firing axe rules, descending by node count.

count.description: Violation node count for this rule across the run.

impact.description: axe-core impact severity for the rule, or null when none was reported.
